page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v5 is an EASv5-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The underlying hardware features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.7 GHz with 32 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing an L3 cache of 32 MB, L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and L1d cache of 32 KB. This instance type does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory performance is particularly notable, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10% and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching the top 25% at 4165.53 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier.

Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and bundled GPUs, which limits its utility for local-disk-heavy tasks or hardware-accelerated graphics. Large-model LLM text generation is a bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation speed scoring in the bottom 10% at 2.47 tokens/sec. Conversely, the high memory capacity and strong database operation benchmarks, including a top 25% ranking in Passmark database and Redis SET operations at 63.15 million operations per second, make this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, in-memory caching, and software compilation.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64as_v5 is an EASv5-family virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, this memory-optimized instance offers a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks place this server in the top 10% for Passmark memory scores and the top 25% for multi-core CPU execution, Redis SET operations, and database operations. Conversely, large-block uncached memory bandwidth and large-model LLM text generation perform in the average and poor tiers, respectively. The server is designed for memory-intensive workloads, including relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, and large-scale software compilation, where high memory density and strong multi-core processing are required.
